text: You shipped your app today. Two hundred views.
But Theo's launch ad hit forty thousand by lunch.
So you open his app. It does half of yours.
Three months ago, you had a job and an idea.
Every night after work, you coded until two.
Until one night, you quit the job to ship it.
But Theo just grins. Views are views, he says. Speed wins.
So you think about an ad too.
But Blip beeps. Problem one. A view is not a person.
Instagram counts a view each time a reel starts. Replays too.
So forty thousand views might be a few thousand people.
But his ad has zero comments.
So, problem two. Nobody shares a demo.
Instagram's boss says sends beat likes for reaching new people.
So people don't share apps. They share stories.
So your story is the bug that almost killed it?
But Theo says post a clean demo. Nobody cares about bugs.
Three nights. One bug. You almost quit.
So Blip is sure. Show the night you almost quit.
But one new comment sits under your post. It's from Theo.
The demo is safe. It looks pro. Nobody shares it.
But the story is scary. Everyone sees you almost failed.
So, one post tonight. Tomorrow, they count.
Comment A for the demo, or B for the story.
